rationale.conceptual: The method is a standard DFT surface adsorption study but requires non-trivial setup of the GaAs(100)-β2(2×4) reconstruction, pseudo-hydrogen passivation, Zn doping, multiple adsorption sites and orientations, work function extraction, and the Hogan dipole analysis; several components must interact correctly.
rationale.execution: The pipeline has ~6-7 stages: slab construction and optimization, isolated species calculations, 10 separate geometry optimizations, and post-processing to extract multiple scored quantities. Dependencies exist and DFT tooling can be finicky, but overall scriptable.

difficulty.reasoning: Standard DFT slab calculations with multiple adsorption configurations; method is well-established but requires careful setup of surface reconstruction, pseudo-potentials, and charge analysis. Pipeline involves many individual jobs and post-processing, but is scriptable and not extremely complex.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Each DFT optimization of a ~50-atom slab requires modest RAM (~few GB), and total runtime is CPU-bound (~2-4 h per configuration); input data is limited to pseudopotentials and structural coordinates.
